transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO - Oceanic), Meera (ML Lead), Jordan (Infra), Ravi (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on model selection for Oceanic's multi-lingual customer support assistant. Main topics: open model comparisons (performance vs cost), required context lengths (32k vs 128k), multilingual handling, and tool-calling / function-calling support. Customer prefers hosted to start but has strict security questions about VPC/private, KMS and audit logs. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send cost worksheet and benchmarks; customer to share prompt sets for eval.

Topics:
- Current stack and constraints
- Model capability needs (multilingual, safety, formatting, tool-calls)
- Context length and KV caching implications
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2/ISO, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot and evaluation criteria

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can we do quick intros? I'm Maya, I'm lead AE on the inference team.
[00:10] Carlos (Oceanic CTO): Hi, Carlos here. We're re-evaluating our stack for the customer support assistant, want to understand model choices and infra options.
[00:17] Meera (ML Lead): Meera, ML lead. Focused on model accuracy, multilingual responses, and hallucination controls.
[00:23] Jordan (Infra): Jordan, infra. I'm looking at network constraints, VPC, and key management.
[00:28] Ravi (PM): Ravi, product. Timeline is Q2 pilot ideally.
[00:33] Liam (Redwood SE): Thanks, great to meet you. Sofia and I will walk through technical tradeoffs and model selection. Quick ask: what are the top success criteria? Latency, cost, or accuracy?
[00:44] Meera: Accuracy first, then latency. We serve global customers in 8 languages, so multilingual models matter. Also need long context — conversation history + docs; sometimes up to 60k tokens in a thread, hoping to support that.
[00:58] Carlos: And we have some PII in transcripts, so data residency and key control are non-negotiable.
[01:05] Maya: Got it. Quick qualifier: are you comfortable starting on Hosted for fast iteration or do you need Dedicated/Private from day one for compliance?
[01:15] Carlos: Prefer to start hosted but with options to move to Dedicated or Private once we're past pilot. If hosted can't give sufficient controls (e.g., KMS integration) then we might push for Private earlier.
[01:27] Sofia (Redwood SE): That lines up with what others do. Hosted gives fastest time to value; Dedicated gives predictable throughput; Private (V P C) gives full network control. We do KMS integrations and audit logging across tiers, but Private gives you customer-managed keys and air-gapped options.
[01:41] Jordan: When you say KMS integrations, is that BYOK? HSM? We need to know for our security team.
[01:47] Liam: Yes, BYOK via customer KMS and HSM options for Private, and dedicated infra can be configured with customer-managed keys. Hosted supports envelope encryption and we have SOC 2 and ISO attestations — we'll send the security pack.
[01:58] Meera: Cool. On models, we're evaluating open models mostly — want to avoid per-call vendor lock. Which families should we be considering for multiling and tool-calling?
[02:08] Sofia: For open models, the big options are Llama-style variants, Mixtral-like, and the newer multilingual LLMs like Mistral / Llama 3 derivatives. For tool-calling, some models have native function-calling support out of the box, others we wrap in deterministic adapters.
[02:23] Carlos: Are there big differences between, say, Llama 3-70B and Mixtral for Spanish/Japanese?
[02:29] Liam: In our internal benchmarks, Llama 3 derivatives tend to be better on instruction-following at scale; Mixtral and Mistral variants often are strong at code and reasoning. For multilingual, the newer models fine-tuned with multilingual corpora beat older Llama-family variants on low-resource languages — but it depends on your languages. We should run your prompt sets.
[02:45] Speaker 1 (transcript auto): um mm
[02:48] Meera: We'll provide Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese prompt sets. Also many of our threads need 32k context; some legal/troubleshooting cases hit 60k. How does Redwood handle 60k?
[02:58] Liam: Two angles — model context window and infra. We support model variants with up to 128k context using window-extended checkpoints. Practically, cost and latency go up linearly with context length unless you use KV cache / prefix caching. Our runtime provides KV caching and prefix compression so repeated doc contexts are cached and we route requests to variants optimized for long-context.
[03:17] Jordan: Does KV cache persist per customer or per model instance? We worried about memory footprint.
[03:22] Sofia: It can be per-customer and per-instance, configurable. There's a tradeoff: larger cache reduces tokens sent repeatedly but needs memory. We can run autoscaling and bounded caches so memory doesn't blow out. We'll share notes on cache sizing for 32k vs 128k.
[03:33] Maya: Another question — tool-calling / function call support. We need the model to call our internal tools (ticket system lookups, KB retrievals). How mature is that?
[03:41] Liam: Function-calling is supported. For hosted, we provide a secure runtime for tool invocation with webhook signing and rate limits. For Dedicated/Private, you can run the tool adapters inside your VPC and Redwood simply returns structured call intents. We also have patterns for safe tool invocation and allow-listing.
[03:57] Carlos: Any concerns about latency when we do external tool calls mid-generation? We need sub-500ms p95 for simple lookups.
[04:04] Liam: If the model decides to call a tool, there's an additional round-trip. Best practice: do tool-calls as part of plan step — precompute lookups or use cached tool outputs. For very low-latency lookups, we recommend colocating the endpoint or using Dedicated with private networking. That said, for simple DB lookups we've seen p95 in 300-600ms with Dedicated in-region.
[04:22] Ravi: Cost — how much more expensive is 128k vs 32k on tokens?
[04:27] Sofia: Cost scales with tokens processed. If you have long contexts but most of it is repeated, caching helps. We'll send a cost comparison worksheet — for raw per-token compute, 128k models can be 3-4x more expensive if you process full windows each request.
[04:40] Speaker 2 (auto): yeah okay
[04:43] Meera: Safety — we need moderation and deterministic responses for policy related flows. Can you run guards and reranking on top?
[04:50] Liam: Yes — we have built-in reranking, safety filters, and could chain a smaller safety model for classification. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model choices to hit cost targets while preserving quality.
[05:00] Carlos: About private deploys — how long to stand up Private? We're thinking 6-8 weeks for pilot.
[05:06] Maya: For Private it's typically 6-12 weeks depending on network and KMS provisioning. Dedicated can be fast if you just reserve capacity, hosted is immediate. For a Q2 pilot, starting hosted or dedicated is common and then migrating to Private for compliance.
[05:19] Jordan: Our security folks will ask for audit logs and SSO integration. Do you support SAML/Okta and detailed audit logs for token-level usage?
[05:26] Sofia: Yes, SAML SSO via Okta, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC and per-token auditing. We retain logs per your retention policy; for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM.
[05:36] Meera: When you benchmark models, do you provide multilingual evals and BLEU-like metrics, or just English?
[05:42] Liam: We do multilingual evals if you provide prompt sets. We run accuracy, safety, and hallucination checks and output confusion matrices. For multilingual, we also check alignment on formatting and locale.
[05:53] Carlos: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI's longer context offerings. Any notable differences?
[05:59] Liam: Anthropic and OpenAI have strong hosted models and function-calling features; the difference with Redwood is we provide a consistent runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and deep observability into per-token cost and latency. Also our model catalog includes vetted open models so you can avoid vendor lock.
[06:16] Ravi: Logistics: pilot scope and success criteria?
[06:19] Meera: Reduce support resolution time by 20%, maintain 95% NPS on canned replies, and handle Spanish/Japanese parity with English. Latency p95 under 600ms for regular responses.
[06:30] Maya: Great. Recap and next steps then. We'll send cost worksheet, security pack, and a benchmarking plan. Can you share the prompt sets by Monday?
[06:40] Meera: Yes, we'll upload by Monday.
[06:42] Maya: Okay, we'll schedule a technical deep-dive where Liam will run through the KV cache sizing and long-context benchmarks. Any final q's?
[06:50] Carlos: One more — are there hard limits on throughput for Dedicated? If we scale to 5k requests per minute during peak, can you handle?
[06:57] Sofia: Dedicated is sized by GPU pools and autoscaling policies; we can provision for predictable throughput and burst capacity. We'll include throughput planning questions in the worksheet.
[07:07] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items discussed.
[07:11] Meera: Thanks.
[07:12] End of call.
